A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HEA study and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and complete appendices. The added Appendix F in v2 shifts the later appendix letters; the corresponding material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original kernel eigensystem measurements, learning curves, sample complexities, MLP training experiments, and robustness studies on synthetic and real datasets.

after.justification: v2 reports original kernel eigensystem and learning-curve experiments, together with MLP training results and appendix robustness studies.

M1.justification: The HEA construction, Gram-Schmidt target decomposition, and KRR prediction procedure remain unchanged. The MLP depth description changes from three total layers to two hidden layers, which alone does not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Gaussian data, CIFAR data, SVHN, ImageNet-32, and the MNIST and Mushroom failure cases. Hermite-polynomial, power-law, and binarized-label tasks remain; the MLP revisions concern settings and results within this coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 9 retains empirical kernel diagonalization, greedy residual fitting, and isotropic-data predictions as comparisons. The evaluated kernel families and MLP regimes also remain. Newly cited concurrent work is discussed rather than added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported default MLP learning rate changes from 0.01 to 0.02. Figure 20 changes the higher-rate condition from 0.5 to 0.1 and the narrow-width condition from 128 to 1024. These are localized setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish precisely which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 20 and 21 revise the MLP hyperparameter and richness sensitivity evidence, including different learning-rate and width conditions. They retain the same questions about learning-time scaling. The KRR ablations and failure analyses in Appendices D and E remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report up to 50 KRR trials, 20 trials for the specified sample-complexity estimates, three trials for the base Gaussian and CIFAR-5m MLP cases, and single trials for further MLP validation. The MLP run-count paragraph is relocated; uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4, 20, and 21 contain revised MLP optimization-time points and displayed result entries. The lazy-regime plot changes substantially in scale, while the stated scaling exponents of 1, 1/2, and approximately 0.4 remain. These are revised results under changed settings, not demonstrated performance gains. The core KRR results are retained.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, theorem statements, and proof arguments are retained, with v1 Appendices H–J corresponding to v2 Appendices I–K. Added prose explains existing eigenspace convergence, assumptions, and asymptotic limits without introducing a new mathematical result or substantive proof revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: predicting KRR learning curves from covariance and target coefficients, proving HEA in two Gaussian limiting cases, and predicting polynomial learning order in feature-learning MLPs.

C2.justification: New Appendix F distinguishes Gaussian input modeling from Gaussian universality in kernel feature space and discusses accumulated approximation errors and the absence of end-to-end formal guarantees. Section 4.1 explains why the limiting eigenvalue predictions remain nontrivial. Figure 21 adds a learning-rate explanation for the elevated constant-mode time.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix G explicitly supplies the synthetic MLP input dimension d = 200 and the lazy-regime base learning rate of 20, and clarifies richness-related learning-rate notation. MLP hyperparameter documentation is revised. The code repository access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wortsman and Loureiro (2025), discussing agreement with their eigenvalue bounds and positioning HEA as justification for replacing dot-product kernels with Hermite kernels. It also adds Caponnetto and De Vito (2007). The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory paragraphs and a standalone assumptions appendix, renumbers subsequent appendices, and makes localized proof-exposition, terminology, and acknowledgment edits. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4, 20, and 21 are redrawn with revised annotations, legends, and axis ranges; figures are relocated and conference headers added. Figure 24 corrects a multiplicity label from 3 to 4. Figure 20 introduces a mismatch between its one-hidden-layer panel label and two-hidden-layer caption.

improvement.justification: The added assumptions discussion and explanations of HEA approximation and limiting behavior make the existing claims easier to assess. Additional MLP settings and concurrent-work positioning improve documentation and context. These limited gains outweigh the new Figure 20 caption inconsistency. The method, proofs, and main KRR evidence remain stable, and revised MLP plots alone do not demonstrate improved performance.
